terms.definition: A very young star still gathering mass, glowing from gravitational contraction rather than fusion.
terms.function: Squeezes and heats up over millions of years until its core is ready to ignite fusion.
terms.whereItIs: The bright center of the model, inside its disk.
terms.whyItMatters: Every star in the sky — including the Sun — began as a protostar.

terms.definition: The process of a gas cloud shrinking under its own gravity, heating up as it shrinks.
terms.function: Powers the protostar's early glow — the squeeze of gravity, not fusion, produces the first light.
terms.whereItIs: Happening inside the core of the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Contraction slowly raises the core temperature all the way up to the ignition threshold.

terms.definition: The flat, spinning disk of gas and dust gathered around a young star.
terms.function: Feeds material onto the star and simultaneously supplies the raw material from which planets form.
terms.whereItIs: The flat disc around the central lump in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Disks exactly like this one built our own solar system — planets grow inside them.

terms.definition: The rule that a spinning object spins faster as it shrinks — the same effect that makes a figure skater speed up when pulling in their arms.
terms.function: Explains both the speeding up of the collapse and why the collapse flattens into a disk.
terms.whereItIs: The physics behind the whole shape of the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It is why all the planets end up orbiting in the same flat plane.

terms.definition: The moment the core's temperature crosses roughly 10 million Kelvin and hydrogen fusion starts sustaining itself.
terms.function: Turns a protostar into a main-sequence star.
terms.whereItIs: The readout plane floating above the core in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Ignition is the real 'birth moment' of a star — everything before it is preparation.
